brief: GS's Friday cross-asset recap: equities fell with the AI trade under renewed pressure (SPX -109bps to 7659, NDX -250bps to 29,187, RTY -166bps to 2721, VIX +3.53 to 19.99); Info Tech and Communication Services led losses, Global Neoclouds extended declines on AI funding/debt worries, while Energy and Nat Gas names were bid. In rates, equities' slide pulled the front-end to a bid, steepening 2s10s and 2s30s 5bps each; swap spreads widened after a primary dealer questionnaire gave no signal of smaller long-end auction sizes. Markets price ~4.75bps of hikes for the October meeting and ~25bps through year-end; next week brings a lighter data calendar, Fed blackout, and 20y/5y TIPS supply. Credit weakened (CDX IG wider, HY lower) as an overnight Itraxx bounce reversed into shorts being reset and CRWV/FMC sold off; desks sold HY vol and bought IG tail downside, ORCL bonds widened on TMT dispersion, and $8bn IG priced with no HY deals. The dollar sagged, driven more by CTA/model long-dollar hedging than discretionary flow, making its pain point harder to call; EUR reclaimed 1.12 (+50bps WTD after a -100bps slide earlier in the week) while JPY was the day's worst G10 performer versus USD despite the broader dollar weakness.
